summary: Intro call focused on SSO/SAML setup, SCIM provisioning, and RBAC/least-privilege model. Customer wants to understand integration with their IdP (Okta), SCIM attribute mapping, role model in Redwood Console, audit logs and retention, KMS/encryption options for Dedicated/Private, and SOC 2/ISO artifacts. Next steps: share SAML metadata, SCIM guide, SOC docs, and schedule follow-up for role mapping and pilot planning.
transcript: [00:00] Lena Park: Hi everyone, thanks for making time. I'm Lena from Redwood, account owner for ClearBank. Marco from our solutions engineering team is with me. how's everyone doing?
[00:08] Sarah Malik: Doing well, thanks. We wanted to walk through SSO, SCIM and how RBAC will map for our teams. We run Okta as our IdP and have fairly tight least-privilege requirements.

[00:18] Marco Diaz: Great, thanks Sarah. Quick agenda: SAML setup and metadata exchange, SCIM provisioning mapping, RBAC roles in Redwood Console, audit logs and retention, encryption and KMS options for Dedicated/Private, and any compliance docs like SOC 2/ISO. Does that cover it?
[00:30] Tom Everett: yes that works. Also want to understand how federated groups map to roles - we have 5 standard groups: eng, sre, sec-ops, product, and auditors.
[00:42] Sarah Malik: and we have a requirement that auditors are read-only and their access must be timeboxed via SAML assertion - short-lived sessions ideally.

[00:55] Marco Diaz: totally. On the SAML side Redwood supports SP-initiated and IdP-initiated flows, cert rollover for metadata, and we have step-by-step Okta docs. We'll send the SP metadata and you can paste it into Okta. For session timing we honor the SAML SessionNotOnOrAfter if provided and we also configurable session TTL in Redwood Console.
[01:20] Priya Nair: how about SCIM? We want user provisioning automated; our HR system syncs to Okta then to Red- uh Redwood via SCIM. Any constraints on attributes?

[01:33] Marco Diaz: SCIM v2 is supported. We map core attributes: userName, givenName, familyName, emails, active, and we can support custom attributes via extension fields. Group provisioning is supported too so you can push Okta groups to Redwood and map groups to roles. We usually recommend using Okta's app provisioning rules to limit sync to the core groups you listed.
[01:55] Evan Cho: is there an option to limit which groups can provision - e.g., only push 'eng' and 'sre' to our production org?

[02:02] Marco Diaz: yes you can set SCIM filters in Okta or in our provisioning configuration. We'll show the exact SCIM filter syntax in the guide. Also note that SCIM operations are audited - create/update/delete events show up in the audit logs with actor info.
[02:18] Sarah Malik: good, we need an audit trail for provisioning changes. What retention do you offer for audit logs?

[02:25] Lena Park: by default hosted plans keep logs for 90 days, Dedicated can be configured to longer retention, and Private deployments can route logs to your SIEM or S3 for arbitrary retention. For the Dedicated pilot we can enable 1 year retention internally if contractually agreed - will need to confirm in the SOW.
[02:45] Tom Everett: and format? Syslog? JSON? We need to ingest into Splunk and our internal ELK stack.

[02:52] Marco Diaz: audit events are JSON with structured fields (timestamp, actor, action, resource, request_id) and we have a streaming export to S3, or direct webhook for a forwarder. We can also support syslog via a small agent in Private but that's per-deployment detail.
[03:10] Sarah Malik: ok. On encryption: our policy requires customer-managed keys for data at rest for production PII workloads. Do you support KMS integration?

[03:18] Marco Diaz: yes, for Private we support HSM/KMS integration (AWS KMS, Cloud HSM) and for Dedicated we support CMKs with envelope encryption. We have docs on key rotation and we never store plaintext keys. For hosted API we manage keys but we can offer Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) for enterprise contracts — we can provide details in the security pack.
[03:40] Sarah Malik: BYOK for hosted would be ideal but likely we'll plan Dedicated/Private for production. What about encryption in transit for internal service-to-service comms?
[03:47] Lena Park: everything is TLS 1.2+ in transit. For Private deployments we can also configure mTLS between services if you require mutual auth.
[03:55] Priya Nair: on RBAC specifics - how are roles modeled in Redwood Console? Is it role-based on the model-level, route-level, or per-organization?

[04:05] Marco Diaz: roles are organization-level with granular permissions that can be scoped to resources like models, projects, or routes. We have built-in roles (Org Admin, Billing, Developer, Viewer) and you can create custom roles mapping to atomic permissions: e.g., start_job, view_logs, manage_keys. Groups from SCIM map to roles and you can do multiple role assignments per user.
[04:28] Tom Everett: can we enforce least-privilege for SRE: only allow read-only view of billing and only access to logs for their region?

[04:35] Marco Diaz: yes permissions are resource-scoped. You can create a role like 'SRE-region-eu' with access only to resources in eu-region and attach it to the Okta group for EU SREs. We also support attribute-based controls for additional constraints.
[04:48] Sarah Malik: what about emergency access: break glass for incident response? We need an auditable flow and temporary escalation with approvals.

[04:57] Marco Diaz: we support time-bound role elevations via the Console and audit logs capture the elevation. For integrations you can tie it into your approval workflow; we can also integrate with systems like PagerDuty or Jira for approval records.
[05:10] Evan Cho: any managed SSO features for multi-tenant accounts? We have multiple business units and want separate orgs or a single org with strict role isolation.

[05:18] Lena Park: you can provision multiple Redwood organizations under your account for strict isolation or use a single org with resource and project-level isolation. We can help design the model during the pilot.
[05:28] Sarah Malik: on SCIM again: how do deprovision events work? If someone leaves the company we trigger a delete in Okta—will Redwood immediately revoke tokens and sessions?

[05:36] Marco Diaz: yes deprovision results in immediate change: account disabled or deleted per your policy. Sessions can be revoked on deprovision; we rely on SCIM active flag and we can optionally call session termination APIs when user is disabled.
[05:48] Tom Everett: what about API keys and service accounts? We want to ensure service keys used by apps aren't left active after someone leaves. Any automation?

[05:55] Marco Diaz: service accounts are separate from user accounts. We recommend short-lived keys and rotating via our API; for Dedicated we can integrate key lifecycle with your secret manager. We also log creation and usage of API keys in the audit logs.
[06:08] Sarah Malik: SOC 2 and ISO: can we get your latest attestation? Also evidence around background checks, pen tests, and change management?

[06:16] Lena Park: yes we'll upload the SOC 2 Type 2 and ISO 27001 certs to the secure share. The security pack includes summary of controls, penetration test summaries (redacted), and our change management process.
[06:28] Jules (Legal): any standard data processing addendum (DPA) and SCCs for EU data? We have EEA residency requirements for some customers and need contractual guarantees.

[06:36] Lena Park: we have a standard DPA and support SCCs and can accommodate data residency via Dedicated or Private deployments in region. For hosted we can pin region choices for enterprise customers - but Dedicated/Private gives you stronger contractual guarantees.
[06:50] Priya Nair: we need to confirm where logs and persisted prompts live. If someone uploads customer PII in a prompt, how is it stored and can we opt out of retention?

[06:58] Marco Diaz: Redwood has configurable data retention. For Dedicated/Private you can set retention to zero for transient data and configure chat/trace retention policies. We also support redaction and callbacks to your own data store for prompt archival. For hosted API, you can opt out of retention under an enterprise contract.
[07:12] Sarah Malik: fine. On SAML cert rotatation - can you support multiple certs for overlap?
[07:18] Marco Diaz: yes SP supports multiple active certificates so you can upload a new cert while the old one is still valid during rollover. We also provide metadata endpoints for automation.
[07:26] Tom Everett: any rate limits on SCIM operations? We will bulk provision about 5k users across groups during migration.
[07:33] Marco Diaz: we have throttling but for migration we can whitelist your provisioning IP and temporarily lift limits in Dedicated for the migration window. We'll coordinate on exact numbers.
[07:45] Sarah Malik: regarding logging integrity, do you support log signing or any tamper-evident mechanisms?

[07:52] Marco Diaz: for Private we can enable immutable logs in S3 with Object Lock, and we also support signed audit exports. For Dedicated we can provide similar guarantees depending on storage config.
[08:05] Priya Nair: what about export of encryption keys if we go Private? Are keys always customer-managed or does Redwood ever have access?

[08:12] Marco Diaz: for customer-managed KMS, Redwood never stores the plaintext key; we use envelope encryption with customer CMK to wrap data keys. For HSM integrations, private key material can be kept in your HSM and only operations performed via API calls.
[08:28] Sarah Malik: good. A compliance question: do you have a dedicated environment for auditors to access logs? We sometimes grant limited read-only S3 access to auditors.

[08:36] Lena Park: auditors can be given timebound read-only access to the audit exports or we can generate attestation packages. We typically prefer S3 exports with temporary credentials scoped to the bucket and object prefix.
[08:47] Tom Everett: what about network restrictions - can we limit console access to our corp VPN or IP allowlist?

[08:55] Marco Diaz: yes, IP allowlisting, SSO session controls, and for Private we can put the control plane behind your VPC. For Dedicated we support IP allowlist on the control plane and mTLS for internal traffic.
[09:08] Sarah Malik: are there RBAC audit reports? e.g., show who changed role bindings and when?
[09:15] Marco Diaz: yes role binding changes are audited with before/after state diffs. You can query audit logs in the Console or export them for SIEM.
[09:26] Evan Cho: do you offer SCIM delta syncs or full re-sync only?
[09:31] Marco Diaz: SCIM supports incremental (PATCH) and list filter operations; we support both delta-based provisioning and full imports as needed.
[09:40] Sarah Malik: minor point: our IdP team calls groups 'app groups' and they've had issues mapping nested groups. How do you handle nested group sync?
[09:48] Marco Diaz: we accept group entries and can flatten nested groups during provisioning; we can also support SCIM group membership expansions on our side depending on your Okta settings.
[09:58] Tom Everett: let's talk about monitoring - do you expose audit stream and metric telemetry for security events?
[10:03] Marco Diaz: yes we expose security metrics (auth failures, provisioning errors, role elevation events) and you can plug into Prometheus/Grafana or forward metrics to your monitoring endpoint.
[10:14] Sarah Malik: any gotchas for SAML assertions size or attributes? We need email and employee-id as required attributes. Also we have an encrypted assertion requirement for some apps.

[10:23] Marco Diaz: we support encrypted assertions and common attributes. We'll include the full attribute list in the SAML guide. For employee-id we recommend using the immutable id field to avoid duplication.
[10:35] Priya Nair: incident response: if there's a data leakage event involving prompts, what's the suggested workflow with Redwood?

[10:42] Lena Park: we have an incident response playbook in the security pack. It includes escalation contacts, notification SLAs, log export steps, and for Private/Dedicated we can provide extended support and direct access for forensic work.
[10:55] Sarah Malik: ok that's helpful. Jules from legal: any contractual SLAs around data deletion requests? We need proof of deletion and certificates of destruction for some datasets.

[11:05] Lena Park: we support deletion requests and can provide audit artifacts showing purge operations. For stronger guarantees we recommend Private or Dedicated with controlled storage that you own or we can configure retention/purge policies to meet requirements.
[11:17] Tom Everett: will you share a sample SAML metadata endpoint and a SCIM schema we can test against in our Okta sandbox?
[11:23] Marco Diaz: yes Marco: I'll share SP metadata, SCIM schema, and a sample Okta application template. Also include recommended group-to-role mapping examples for your 5 groups.

[11:35] Sarah Malik: we'd like to see example mapping: auditors->Viewer read-only; sec-ops->can-view-logs and start incident jobs; eng->deploy-models only to dev/prod? we need to refine that with the matrix.
[11:47] Marco Diaz: we'll provide a starter RBAC matrix and a suggested mapping to your groups. You can then tweak permissions in Console or via API.
[11:55] Priya Nair: on token revocation - do you have an API to revoke user sessions or tokens programmatically?
[12:01] Marco Diaz: yes session and token revocation APIs exist. We can also expose webhook hooks for deprovision events to trigger revocation in downstream systems.
[12:12] Sarah Malik: any integration with enterprise ID proofing or SCIM provisioning workflows that include manager approval?

[12:19] Marco Diaz: that's normally handled by your IdP or HR layer. Our SCIM interface will respect the state Okta pushes (active/disabled) and we can accept any custom attribute to represent manager approval if you want to gate provisioning.
[12:30] Tom Everett: can Redwood support SAML signed requests from SP? we sign AuthNRequests?
[12:36] Marco Diaz: we support both signed AuthNRequests and signed assertions. We'll document the key/cert requirements.
[12:44] Sarah Malik: one last question on multi-region keys: if we run Dedicated across regions, can we have regionally-scoped CMKs?
[12:51] Marco Diaz: yes region-specific CMKs and region-bound encryption is supported for Dedicated/Private; we'll document the architecture choices.

[13:00] Lena Park: okay let's recap next steps: Marco will share SAML metadata, SCIM guide, and sample Okta app; I'll upload SOC 2 / ISO docs; Sarah will share RBAC matrix. We'll set a follow-up to walk through the SCIM mapping and pilot plan. Any objections?
[13:14] Sarah Malik: none. One ask: can you include a sample audit log extract showing provisioning create/update/delete events?
[13:21] Marco Diaz: yes will include sample logs and a sample mapping to Splunk ingestion.
[13:29] Jules (Legal): and please include your DPA and SCCs in the doc bundle.
[13:34] Lena Park: will do. We'll get these to you by end of day tomorrow for Lena and Marco to follow up. thanks all for a solid session.
[13:42] Sarah Malik: thanks everyone.
